extracted.intended_audience: female readers/volunteer charitable workers and tract-distributors (readers of The Girl's Own Paper); also amateur music teachers/composers mentioned in notices
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for women volunteers on collecting and sending donated toys, books, and religious literature to schoolgirls and native ladies in India, and on effective distribution of tracts and books among working people; also contains short evaluative guidance for composers/teachers in the 'Notices of New Music'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Song setting should suit text and be accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: “A sympathetic, easy setting of the sad words by Helen M. Waitman.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settings should be sympathetic to the words, easy to sing, and published in appropriate keys for singers (example: published in F and A flat). Ensure vocal compass suits typical singers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompaniment needs contrast and rests
rubrics_metrics.description: “The violin accompaniment, charming as it is, would have been much more so, had it been broken up a little more. There is no rest for it, and this destroys much of its effect.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unceasing accompaniment lines; introduce rests and breaks to preserve effect and highlight the vocal line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide alternate instrument options/transpositions
rubrics_metrics.description: “The same part has been transposed an octave for a violoncello.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider transpositions or alternate parts for other common instruments (e.g., cello) to expand usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for student violin music (fingerings/bowings)
rubrics_metrics.description: “They are simple, effective, and melodious. As they are so evidently intended for young people, we are surprised that the violin part is neither fingered nor bowed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing/arranging for young or amateur violinists, include fingering and bowing indications to aid learning and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Piano pieces for amateurs should be graceful and sympathetic
rubrics_metrics.description: “If the others are as delightful as Nos. 4 (Lullaby) and 5 (Welcome) ... these romances are the most graceful and sympathetic works for the piano ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose piano pieces for amateurs that are melodious, graceful, and sympathetic in treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dance pieces must sustain character/excitement
rubrics_metrics.description: “A very characteristic specimen of this phrenzied dance. The excitement is well sustained to the close.” (Tarantella)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dance pieces should maintain their characteristic energy or mood throughout to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local colouring and graceful subject in national/dance pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: “Containing what Mr. Corder would call ‘distinct local colouring,’ and developing a graceful subject.” (Spanish Waltz)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authentic local color and develop a graceful main subject; ensure title/presentation matches the work (note: comment on title language mismatch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangements of older works should be made interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: “An interesting relic ... arranged by Edwin M. Lott for the piano.” (Gavotte by Ariosti)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arranging historical pieces, present them in a way that highlights interest and accessibility for modern players.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical studies (arpeggios) should be pedagogically useful
rubrics_metrics.description: “An extremely useful collection of these technical passages. ... The arrangement ... is founded on the well-known work of Charles Chaulieu.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile technical exercises with pedagogical lineage and clear organization; base collections on established methods to ensure usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organ writing requires contrast in pedal use
rubrics_metrics.description: “Amongst others is the fact that the pedals are used without intermission from beginning to end, augmenting a want of contrast and variety already too apparent in both pieces.” (Two Andantes for organ)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid continuous pedal usage that removes contrast; design organ parts with variety between manual and pedal for tonal contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's piano methods should be graded and child-centred
rubrics_metrics.description: “A most important addition ... the Child Pianist, divided into grades and steps, and combining in a thoughtful and systematic way a little theory and a little practice, never forcing a child, and never letting the head get in front of the hands or vice versâ.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design methods in clear graded steps, balance theory and practice, avoid forcing students, prioritize practical hand development before theoretical abstraction; include pupil-teacher duets and a Teacher’s Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include pupil–teacher duets and a Teacher’s Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: “Accompanying these steps with their capital duets for pupil and teacher ... we have a Teacher’s Guide to the Child Pianist, an assistance to young teachers, and an essential explanation to the exercises and method.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide duet material for supervised practice and a teacher’s guide to explain exercises, progression, and pedagogy for novice instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dance/entr'acte pieces should be charming, graceful, well-constructed
rubrics_metrics.description: “Really charming and graceful as piano pieces, for little entr’actes at readings, or between charades; ... the Postscript Polka, the latter being especially happy in its construction.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For short interlude pieces, prioritize charm, graceful melody, and tight construction suitable for short performance contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish songs in keys appropriate to voice types
rubrics_metrics.description: “Yellow Roses we can recommend as a pretty ballad ... It is published in every necessary key.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish vocal music in multiple keys to accommodate different voice ranges and to increase accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose songs with suitable compass and aware harmony
rubrics_metrics.description: “A song of moderate compass, possessing much musical feeling, and the originality ... A curious, not very vocal, effect is produced by the diminished fourth ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write songs with an appropriate vocal compass and be mindful of harmonic choices (e.g., unusual intervals) that may create awkward vocal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer books/magazines over single tracts for distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: “The magazine or book is more acceptable than the mere tract, and when regularly supplied is often eagerly accepted and expected.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distributing religious literature, favour magazines or small books rather than single leaflets; regular supply builds readership and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribute on Sundays to public servants who cannot attend worship
rubrics_metrics.description: “They are particularly welcomed on Sunday, when policemen, cabmen, firemen, and other public servants who cannot attend a place of worship, say they like to have something to read when they are off duty.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target distribution times (e.g., Sundays) when working public servants are on duty and would appreciate reading material during quiet moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pictorial and child-friendly material; supply 'something for the little ones'
rubrics_metrics.description: “The pictures always attract ... ‘I like a whole story that I can read all through,’ said one ... ‘The Child’s Companion’ ... ‘something for the little ones’ is a boon.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include illustrated material and complete short stories for family reading; provide specific children's titles that can be read aloud or lent among families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be kind, discreet, and cheerful in distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: “Though a kindly discretion, and, perhaps, a cheerful manner are needed for their distribution.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach recipients with tact and a cheerful disposition; avoid moralizing tones that may be perceived as 'cant' and repel readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and handle rebuffs respectfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported rebuffs such as 'No, thankee. I don’t want one.' and 'Because I hate cant' appear in accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect refusals; respond courteously, avoid argument where unproductive, and move on to receptive audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target workplaces and social contexts where readers are reachable
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: railway officials, newsboys, navvies, laundries, fire brigade, coffee-stalls, gipsy encampments, barges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute literature in settings where people have leisure or small regular breaks (laundries, stations, coffee-stalls) and among groups likely to share reading material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tangible rewards/prizes to encourage school attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: “If it is the time for a prize-giving ... she chooses some suitable things, which are placed on a table and distributed with the usual ceremony ... Whether or not it is a prize occasion, Mrs. Brander gives Christmas cards to the scholars that have attended for a month with regularity.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select attractive small prizes (dolls, cards, boxes) to incentivize attendance and punctuality; leave packets with local teachers to use as future rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable donated items and qualitative prefs for Indian schoolgirls
rubrics_metrics.description: “The dolls should be of composition or china, not of very soft wax. It is not necessary that their clothes should take off and on, though for large dolls this is an advantage. The Indian children are very pleased to have small boxes with lock and key, to keep their bangles in, and they like bags too. At Calcutta many of the ladies read English, so that interesting books are of use, if not very difficult. I shall be able to inform the donors ... I need presents not only for Madras but for other places ... old Christmas cards (with or without writing upon them).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect durable dolls (composition or china), small lockable boxes, bags, simple but interesting books (where recipients read English), and Christmas cards/scrapbooks. For large dolls detachable clothing is a bonus but not required. Keep donors informed of distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with local contacts and be mindful of denominational sensitivities
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories such as the Polish Jewish family: aid was accepted in hunger; later the family was placed under a charitable Jewish lady; comment that 'it is well that Jew and Gentile should meet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with local partners and respect recipients’ religious/denominational preferences; coordinate where other groups serve the same communities to avoid friction and respect cultural sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use colporteurs/paid distribution channels and combine relief with literature
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have occasionally fallen in with the regular colporteurs, and been convinced of the good done by the sale of their religious literature. ... One evening at dusk we encountered a glazier ... a trifle for them and refreshment for him opened his heart...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider employing or cooperating with local colporteurs and distribution points (coffee-stalls); pairing small acts of relief (food/refreshment) with literature can open opportunities for further contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide material appropriate to literacy levels and encourage education
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of men who had little schooling; recommendation to go to night-school; 'It is strange that one still meets with people comparatively young who cannot read. Much of their religious knowledge is often due to hymns.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select simple, readable materials for low-literacy audiences; promote night schools and literacy programs alongside literature distribution; use hymns and oral reading where literacy is low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply serial or regular literature to build readership
rubrics_metrics.description: “The supply rarely answers the demand ... The supply of 'The Child’s Companion' is welcomed and passed on.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for ongoing provision (monthly/regular) so recipients expect and share periodicals; serial literature fosters a reading community and multiplies impact.
